text: The object is a finite abelian group with a symmetric pairing taking rational values modulo integers, as in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). Storing x ↦ (y ↦ b(x,y)) as two additive maps enforces additivity in both arguments. Degenerate pairings are allowed; nondegeneracy is a separate condition. The bilinear conversion preserves every value. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L130) passes.
The integer-bilinear conversion evaluates to the stored pairing.

Treating a finite bilinear module as a set means taking its original underlying abelian group, with the same elements, addition and finiteness. This matches the carrier of a finite form in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). No quotient or change of group occurs; the original pairing and its bilinear presentation accept the identical elements. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L130) passes.
Pairing and bilinear conversion have the identical carrier and evaluation.

Nondegeneracy says that pairing against elements gives every additive ℚ/ℤ-valued character exactly once. Because the group is finite, its character group has the same size, so injectivity suffices. This matches nondegeneracy for the forms of [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). Finiteness comes from the module itself; degenerate forms remain allowed as separate objects. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L148) passes.
Finite duality identifies perfectness with an injective adjoint.

An isometry is an isomorphism of the underlying abelian groups that preserves the value of the pairing on every pair of elements. This is isomorphism of finite symmetric forms as considered in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). Degenerate pairings are permitted. The inverse group isomorphism also preserves the pairing and undoes the original map. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L362) passes.
The bundled inverse undoes the original isometry.

Nondegeneracy is stored as bijectivity of the actual adjoint x ↦ b(x,−), so its injectivity component separates elements by their pairing characters. This is the radical-zero condition for the finite forms of [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). Its native use proves that pairing-preserving maps from a nondegenerate source are injective. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L252) passes.
A nondegenerate source forces a pairing-preserving morphism to be injective.

Allowing an isometry to act as an invertible function uses its existing group isomorphism and inverse, with their original cancellation laws. These are the maps underlying isomorphisms of finite forms in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). The pairing-preservation condition adds no extra map; the native inverse-application identity checks the direction on actual elements. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L362) passes.
The inverse function acts on the same carrier and cancels the forward map.

A nondegenerate pairing identifies the group with all additive ℚ/ℤ-valued characters by sending x to the function y ↦ b(x,y). This is the perfect-pairing identification for the finite forms of [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). The inverse is obtained from bijectivity; its construction does not alter the explicitly specified forward map. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L168) passes.
The forward map is exactly x ↦ A.pairing x.

The character assigned to x by the nondegenerate-pairing identification is exactly y ↦ b(x,y). Thus the equality fixes its value at every second argument simultaneously, and does not introduce a different identification with the dual group. This matches the finite-form convention of [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6); nondegeneracy ensures the map is bijective. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L160) passes.
The underlying adjoint really is bijective under the stated hypothesis.

The second argument is evaluated by an additive character, giving b(x,y+z)=b(x,y)+b(x,z) in ℚ/ℤ. This is second-variable biadditivity in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6), with no nondegeneracy hypothesis. The stored character law also handles zero, as the native right-zero theorem confirms for the same codomain and carrier. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L96) passes.
The same character evaluates zero to zero.

Natural scalar multiplication means repeated addition in the finite group and in ℚ/ℤ. Symmetry and the character homomorphism law yield b(nx,y)=n·b(x,y), the integer-biadditivity convention of [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6) restricted to natural scalars. The statement includes n=0; the native left-zero theorem checks that boundary. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L91) passes.
The n=0 boundary has the expected vanishing pairing.

The adjoint is an additive homomorphism, so its value at zero is the zero character and evaluation is zero in ℚ/ℤ. This is exactly the zero consequence of biadditivity in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). It holds equally for degenerate forms and for the trivial group; second-variable zero is checked independently. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L96) passes.
The independent character law gives vanishing in the other argument.

This presents the same pairing as an integer-bilinear map with values in ℚ/ℤ, matching [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). Additivity gives compatibility with every integer scalar in each argument. The notation AddCircle(1:ℚ) means rational values modulo integers. It asserts no rational scalar action on the finite group, and evaluation preserves the original pairing. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L130) passes.
The conversion changes packaging while retaining every pairing value.

The asserted bijectivity is exactly the definition of nondegeneracy applied to the stored pairing adjoint. Its codomain is the complete ℚ/ℤ-character group. For the finite forms of [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6) this supplies the additive equivalence with the character dual, whose native evaluation theorem verifies the forward map explicitly. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L168) passes.
The equivalence produced from bijectivity uses the original adjoint.

Surjectivity says every ℚ/ℤ-valued additive character is pairing against some element. It is the second component of the perfect adjoint hypothesis, appropriate for the finite forms of [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). The constructed adjoint equivalence evaluates to that very pairing character, confirming that surjectivity concerns the full character module. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L168) passes.
The character-dual equivalence has the stated adjoint as forward map.

An isometry and its underlying group isomorphism send each element to exactly the same image. This equality ensures that forgetting the pairing-preservation certificate does not change the map, as required for isomorphisms of the finite forms in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). Forgetting invertibility as well also retains that identical function. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L308) passes.
Forgetting bijectivity preserves the same pointwise function.

An isometry automatically acts as a group isomorphism: it preserves addition and has the inverse already supplied in its definition. This exposes the ordinary group-map component of isomorphisms of finite forms in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). The native forgetful-map identity confirms that the resulting additive homomorphism is precisely the original group isomorphism. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L312) passes.
The forgotten additive homomorphism is precisely the stored additive equivalence.

The equality evaluates the target pairing on both images and returns the source pairing in ℚ/ℤ, directly exposing the structure’s preservation field. This is the form-preserving requirement for isomorphisms in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). Its native use transfers nondegeneracy across the isometry, with the reverse implication obtained from the inverse. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L402) passes.
Preservation and the inverse imply invariance of nondegeneracy.

An isometry is determined by its underlying group isomorphism: the additional condition merely certifies preservation of the pairing and carries no further mathematical data. Thus two isometries with the same group map are equal, as expected for the finite forms in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). The native equality criterion states this equivalence explicitly. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L277) passes.
Equality of underlying additive equivalences is equivalent to equality of isometries.

The reverse implication uses equality of finite cardinalities between the group and its ℚ/ℤ-character module; injectivity therefore gives surjectivity. The forward implication is immediate from the definition. This identifies the perfect-adjoint formulation with ordinary nondegeneracy for the finite symmetric forms of [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6), including the trivial group. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L144) passes.
The reverse implication explicitly invokes the finite character-cardinality identity.

Additivity of the adjoint gives equality of characters, and evaluation at the second argument gives the displayed equality in ℚ/ℤ. This is first-variable biadditivity in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6) with no nondegeneracy assumption. Together with the independent right-additivity theorem it provides precisely the two additive laws used by the bilinear conversion. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L104) passes.
The second-variable law supplies the other half of biadditivity.

The additive adjoint sends the inverse of an element to the inverse character; evaluation gives b(−x,y)=−b(x,y) in ℚ/ℤ. This is the expected integer-biadditivity consequence for the finite forms of [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). The native right-negation theorem checks the analogous operation in the other argument, including torsion elements. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L113) passes.
Negation in the second argument gives the same codomain inverse.

Presenting the pairing as an integer-bilinear map leaves its value at every pair of elements unchanged. The target is still ℚ/ℤ, in the convention of [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6); no representative or rescaling is chosen. The native symmetric-orthogonality theorem uses this equality to transfer vanishing between the two argument orders. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L135) passes.
Symmetry of the stored pairing transfers to the converted bilinear map.

The finite character module has exactly as many elements as the carrier; the source applies this cardinality identity to upgrade an injective adjoint to a bijective one. This justifies the perfect-pairing formulation of nondegeneracy for the finite forms of [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). Finiteness of the two groups alone would not suffice. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L148) passes.
The resulting equivalence exposes both directions of the nondegeneracy criterion.

For each first argument, the pairing is an additive character, whose value at zero is zero in ℚ/ℤ. This is the right-zero consequence of the biadditivity convention in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). It requires no nondegeneracy and includes the trivial carrier; the independent left-zero theorem confirms the complementary argument boundary. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L91) passes.
The adjoint sends zero to the zero character.

A morphism is a homomorphism of the underlying abelian groups preserving all pairing values in ℚ/ℤ, the finite-form convention of [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). It need not be bijective. The native theorem proves injectivity when its source is nondegenerate; this hypothesis is additional, since the definition itself also permits degenerate source pairings. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L252) passes.
Pairing preservation forces injectivity under source nondegeneracy alone.

If two images agree, pairing preservation makes their source pairing characters agree on every element. Nondegeneracy of the source then identifies the original elements. This is the expected injectivity property of morphisms preserving the finite forms of [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6); the target needs no nondegeneracy or equal-cardinality hypothesis. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L205) passes.
The exact preservation equality supplies all source-character evaluations.

A morphism acts on elements by its original group homomorphism. Two morphisms with the same function are equal: the extra pairing-preservation condition contributes no further map or mathematical data. This realizes maps of finite forms in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6) on their original groups; the native identity confirms agreement with the stored homomorphism. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L201) passes.
The stored additive homomorphism and the coercion have identical functions.

The theorem directly exposes the morphism’s defining equality b_B(fx,fy)=b_A(x,y), with values in ℚ/ℤ as in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). Both arguments are transported by the same additive map. Its native use proves injectivity from source nondegeneracy; neither surjectivity of the morphism nor nondegeneracy of the target is built into preservation. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L252) passes.
The preservation equality detects equal images when the source is nondegenerate.

Here reflexivity means that b(x,y)=0 implies b(y,x)=0. The source derives this by symmetry after evaluating the ℤ-bilinear conversion, exactly the symmetric-orthogonality convention for finite forms in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). The docstring states that meaning explicitly; it does not assert vanishing of b(x,x) or require nondegeneracy. Published [control](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Basic.lean#L130) passes.
The converted map evaluates to the same symmetric pairing.

The group consists of pairs (x,y), and its quadratic value is q_A(x)+q_B(y). This is the orthogonal direct sum, implemented by Mathlib’s [quadratic product](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Prod.lean#L54); its pairing is the sum of the two pairings, with zero mixed terms. For two finite abelian groups, direct product and direct sum give this same construction. Existing [check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Quadratic.lean#L495) passes, [check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Quadratic.lean#L499) passes.
Quadratic values add componentwise.
Pairing values have no mixed terms.

This keeps the original bijective additive map and its inverse, and regards it as preserving the polar pairing. Preservation follows by expanding b(x,y)=q(x+y)−q(x)−q(y). Thus a quadratic [isometric equivalence](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/IsometryEquiv.lean#L38) gives an isomorphism of bilinear forms without any change of group or values; no nondegeneracy assumption is needed. Existing [check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Quadratic.lean#L328) passes.
The underlying group isomorphism is unchanged.

This keeps the same finite group and replaces the values q(x) and b(x,y) by their negatives in ℚ/ℤ. Negating the [quadratic-map definition](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L146) negates its polar, so the compatibility remains exact. This is negation of the form, not replacement of x by −x: quadratic homogeneity instead gives q(−x)=q(x). Existing [check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Quadratic.lean#L462) passes, [check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Quadratic.lean#L466) passes.
The quadratic value, rather than its argument, is negated.
The polar pairing is negated as well.

This takes a subgroup H as its underlying finite group and evaluates the original quadratic map on its elements, exactly Mathlib’s [quadratic restriction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L250). Its polar is the original pairing restricted to H×H. No quotient is taken. The restricted pairing may be degenerate even when the original pairing is nondegenerate. Existing [check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Quadratic.lean#L416) passes, [check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Quadratic.lean#L421) passes.
The restricted quadratic value equals the original value.
Both pairing arguments are included in the original group.

Restricting q to a subgroup and then taking its polar gives the same bilinear module as first taking the polar and then restricting both arguments. This follows directly from the [quadratic restriction](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/Basic.lean#L250) and b(x,y)=q(x+y)−q(x)−q(y). Both constructions use the actual subgroup and its unchanged addition; the equality includes their pairings. Existing [check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Quadratic.lean#L421) passes.
The restricted pairing evaluates on the original elements.

A quadratic isomorphism preserves the polar pairing. If a target element pairs to zero with every target element, its inverse image pairs to zero with every source element, hence is zero. This preserves nondegeneracy as defined in [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). Bijectivity of the isometry is essential; a merely preserving map would not suffice. Existing [check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Quadratic.lean#L337) passes.
Applying the inverse gives the converse implication.

Forgetting the quadratic information before or after taking the underlying group isomorphism gives exactly the same map and inverse. The [isometric equivalence](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/QuadraticForm/IsometryEquiv.lean#L38) stores only one such group isomorphism. The extra equations certify preservation of forms; they do not select another map or replace equality by an abstract existence statement. Existing [check](https://github.com/TauCetiProject/TauCeti/blob/b257e0ff255355b2b692c1311d061d2b4dc84e53/TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/FiniteBilinearModule/Quadratic.lean#L298) passes.
The related forgetful operation preserves the identical additive map.

The pairing on the product adds the two component pairings. Testing against (u,0) and (0,v) shows that its zero-pairing elements are exactly pairs of zero-pairing elements in the factors. Therefore its radical is zero precisely when both radicals are zero, matching [Nikulin §1.2](https://www.mathnet.ru/php/getFT.phtml?jrnid=im&option_lang=eng&paperid=1677&what=fullteng#page=6). Nondegeneracy remains an explicit property, not part of the product definition. Lean uses the same definition for semirings and permits nonassociative multiplication on both sides. Preservation of one matters: a constant-zero map into a nontrivial ring is excluded, even though it preserves addition and multiplication. Compared with [the reference](https://ftp.gwdg.de/pub/EMIS/journals/TAC/volumes/28/4/28-04.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Hom/Defs.lean#L308).

The identity ring homomorphism sends each element to itself and consequently preserves addition, multiplication, zero and one. This is the usual identity morphism for semirings and rings. Its construction also works without multiplicative associativity and for the zero ring, exactly as the stated hypotheses permit. Compared with [the reference](https://ftp.gwdg.de/pub/EMIS/journals/TAC/volumes/28/4/28-04.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Ring/Hom/Defs.lean#L548).

An additive monoid homomorphism preserves addition and zero: f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y) and f(0)=0. Lean states this using only the supplied operations and distinguished zeros, without requiring associativity. For ordinary additive monoids it is the standard definition; preserving addition alone need not preserve zero when cancellation is unavailable. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Hom/Defs.lean#L144).

An additive homomorphism is a function satisfying f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y). Only the two addition operations are assumed, so the definition also covers nonassociative structures. No zero is supplied or required to be preserved. The nonunital notation means zero preservation is omitted, rather than prohibited. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Hom/Defs.lean#L114).

A zero-preserving map is a function between sets with designated zeros, satisfying f(0)=0. This is preservation of a distinguished constant, the simplest case of a structure-preserving map. Neither set needs addition or multiplication, and preserving zero alone implies no injectivity, surjectivity or further algebraic compatibility. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Hom/Defs.lean#L85).

This property says that every function in a specified family preserves addition and zero. On additive monoids these are exactly the homomorphism laws. It also applies when only addition and designated zeros are supplied. It does not claim that the family contains every homomorphism, or even that the family is nonempty. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Hom/Defs.lean#L158).

This property says that every function in a specified family preserves addition: f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y). It is the usual operation-preservation condition, isolated from associativity and zero preservation. The family may contain only some additive maps, and it may be empty; no map is constructed by the assertion. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Hom/Defs.lean#L126).

This property requires every function in a specified family to send the designated zero to zero. It expresses preservation of a constant without imposing any binary operation. The family need not contain all such maps and may be empty; the assertion itself neither selects a function nor requires injectivity. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Hom/Defs.lean#L95).

A zero-preserving map sends zero to zero. The theorem exposes exactly that assumed preservation law for any represented family of such maps. No additive or multiplicative structure is needed, and no injectivity assumption is hidden. The two zeros belong respectively to the domain and codomain. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Hom/Defs.lean#L234).

An addition-preserving map satisfies f(x+y)=f(x)+f(y), with addition taken in the domain on the left and codomain on the right. The theorem exposes the defining preservation law. Associativity, commutativity, zero and cancellation are unnecessary, so the statement applies beyond monoids without silently strengthening its assumptions. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Hom/Defs.lean#L326).

In a commutative multiplication, a*b=b*a. The theorem states exactly the assumed commutativity law for two arbitrary elements. It requires no associativity, identity, cancellation or inverses. Consequently it applies to any commutative binary operation, including examples that are not semigroups or monoids. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Semigroup.lean#L258).

The zeroth natural power of any monoid element is the identity: a^0=1. This is the empty-product convention used in repeated multiplication. The base need not be invertible or nonzero; where the monoid also has a zero, the same convention therefore gives 0^0=1. Compared with [the reference](https://www.irif.fr/~jep/PDF/MPRI/MPRI.pdf) and the [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Monoid.lean#L407).

A σ-compact space is one covered by a sequence of compact subsets, exactly Semmes’s definition. The property is asserted for the whole underlying space, without a Hausdorff or local-compactness assumption. Finite covers and the empty space are included, since the sequence may repeat sets or consist entirely of empty sets. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L142).

A subset is σ-compact when it equals the union of a sequence of compact subsets of the ambient space. Equality ensures each covering set lies inside the specified subset, as in Semmes’s definition. The sets need not be closed or nested, and empty or finite unions are included. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L32).

For a σ-compact space, this chooses one increasing compact cover. Starting from any countable compact cover, stage n is the union of its sets numbered zero through n, inclusive. Finite unions remain compact and the total union is unchanged. The choice is not canonical, matching the ordinary existence of such covers. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L204).

The chosen increasing compact sets cover every point of the σ-compact space. Replacing the original cover by finite initial unions preserves its total union, so this is equality with the whole space. Equivalently, each point belongs to some finite stage; no closure or limiting membership is involved. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L210).

Every stage of the chosen increasing cover is compact because it is a finite union of compact sets from the original cover. This is Semmes’s finite-union principle applied to the construction. It includes stage zero and requires neither Hausdorffness nor a claim that these compact subsets are closed. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L207).

A subset is σ-compact in its ambient space exactly when it is a σ-compact space with the inherited subspace topology. Each compact piece has the same compactness in either setting, and the covering equality is unchanged. This follows from Semmes’s subspace compactness principle; the subset need not be closed. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L174).

The range of a continuous map from a σ-compact space is σ-compact. Apply the map to each compact piece of a countable cover: continuity makes each image compact, and their union is exactly the range. The conclusion concerns the image alone, so surjectivity onto the target is unnecessary. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L165).

Saying that the whole underlying set is σ-compact is equivalent to saying that the space is σ-compact. Both formulations require a sequence of compact subsets whose union contains every point, as in Semmes’s definition. They use the same topology and introduce no additional separation, nonemptiness or local-compactness assumption. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L147).

The product of two σ-compact spaces is σ-compact in the product topology. Choose increasing compact covers in both factors and take their stagewise products. These products are compact; any pair lies in one by taking the larger of its two stage indices. Empty factors are allowed. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L226).

A product of finitely many σ-compact spaces is σ-compact. Choose increasing compact covers in the factors and take their products at each stage. Finiteness lets one index dominate the finitely many coordinate indices, giving a cover by compact sets. The empty index set gives a singleton product. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L232).

A closed embedding into a σ-compact space has σ-compact domain. Intersect each compact covering piece with the closed image, then transfer it to the domain through the homeomorphism onto that image. The resulting compact pieces cover the domain. Closedness of the image is explicit, while Hausdorffness is unnecessary. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L261).

A space with a countable topological basis and arbitrarily small compact neighborhoods is σ-compact. Choose a compact neighborhood at each point; second countability gives a countable subcover of their interiors, hence a countable compact cover. This matches Semmes’s criterion, and no Hausdorff assumption is needed. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L187).

A compact exhaustion is a sequence of compact sets covering the space, with each stage contained in the interior of the next. These are precisely the conditions realized by Semmes’s nested-cover construction. Interior containment is stronger than mere inclusion, but need not be strict; the first stage need not be empty. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L323).

A σ-compact space in which every point has a compact neighborhood admits a compact exhaustion. Enlarge each compact stage to a compact neighborhood and include the next covering piece. This is Semmes’s recursive construction, requiring neither Hausdorffness nor arbitrarily small compact neighborhoods. The chosen exhaustion is not canonical. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L418).

Every point of a space with a compact exhaustion belongs to some stage. This follows directly from the covering equality in the definition, as in Semmes’s nested-cover construction. The conclusion gives an existence witness, not a distinguished first stage, and needs no separate local-compactness or separation hypothesis. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L368).

Each stage of a compact exhaustion lies in the interior of its successor. Thus every point already covered has a neighborhood inside the next compact stage, exactly the nesting in Semmes’s construction. The indices are natural numbers, and n+1 means the next stage; the containment need not be strict. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/SigmaCompact.lean#L353).

A Lindelöf space is one whose every open cover has a countable subcover, allowing finite or empty subcovers. The stored definition instead uses cluster points of nontrivial filters closed under countable intersections. The source proves equivalence with the open-cover condition, so it agrees with Semmes’s definition without separation assumptions. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Lindelof.lean#L485).

Assign a neighborhood U(x) to each point of a Lindelöf subset s. Countably many of these neighborhoods cover s, with their centers still chosen in s. Taking interiors gives an open cover, to which Semmes’s definition applies. The neighborhoods themselves need not be open, and an empty subset is allowed. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Lindelof.lean#L170).

Every subset of a space with a countable topological basis is Lindelöf, matching Semmes’s Corollary3.6.15. A cover can be refined using countably many basis elements, and one covering set is selected for each relevant basis element. Thus the conclusion applies to all subspaces, including nonclosed and empty subsets. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Lindelof.lean#L729).

Every σ-compact space is Lindelöf. Given an open cover, choose finitely many covering sets for each compact piece of a countable compact cover. Their countable union still covers the space, exactly the implication in Semmes §5.5. No local-compactness or Hausdorff assumption is needed, and the empty space is included. [Semmes](https://math.rice.edu/~semmes/math443b.pdf); [pinned source](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4/blob/2cabef97b63d3275776b8b060d802de6a6fa1055/Mathlib/Topology/Compactness/Lindelof.lean#L535).
